Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 95, English)
The Third Eye Batch: Dabna, the Second-Chapter Sadhna, and the Teaching on Dimensions

This session is an advanced "Thir d Eye" (T eesri Aankh) batch training session, opening with a brief individual note, a warning about the seriousness of an ongoing 1 1-day sadhna, a sankalp (r esolve) r oll call for the batch's second chapter of practice, and then a long, technical lectur e on chakras, dimensions, kundalini shakti, and how mantras function acr oss planes of existence — illustrated thr oughout using a devotee named Akhilesh as a running example. This session includes meaningful back-and-forth (student questions, a scolding exchange about enthusiasm, and a closing sankalp r equest), so it is pr esented as a 3-part document, though Part III is comparatively short given how much of this session is dir ect instruction.

1. Opening Note: An Individual's Kaal Sarp Dosh (Continuing Fr om a Prior Conversation) The session opens mid-conversation with the speaker telling an unnamed devotee that their kaal sarp dosh (a specific astrological af fliction) is the reason their ef forts have not been coming to completion, and that this dosh will need to be addressed through further practice.

2. Warning: This Sadhna Is Not a Game — Do Not Leave Your Designated Spot The speaker warns devotees currently undertaking this practice while traveling not to treat it lightly , describing it as an extremely intense sadhna, and instructing them not to leave their designated place of practice.
3. Warning: You Will Be Tested in Every Way The speaker tells devotees they will be tested throughout this sadhna, and that if they carry fear or doubt, that will become apparent through the process.

4. Teaching: Understanding "Dabna" (Dr eam Paralysis) as a Spiritual Test The speaker explains the phenomenon of "dabna" — a dream state in which a person realizes they are dreaming, wants to wake up or get out, but cannot — describing this specifically as what "dabna" (being pressed/stuck) means in the context of this sadhna.

5. Sankalp Roll Call: Attendance for the Third Eye Batch's Second Chapter Sadhna The speaker leads a formal sankalp (resolve) session, calling a long roll of devotees' names to confirm attendance and commitment before beginning the second chapter of this batch's sadhna, distinguishing between "old batch" practitioners (whose powers are being renewed) and "new batch" practitioners (who will be checked from the beginning).

6. Teaching: Your Guru Is Your Tattva — Never Deceive Your Guru The speaker teaches that a devotee's guru is their spiritual essence (tattva), and warns that deceiving one's guru, or holding any hidden dishonesty ("khot") in one's mind during this sadhna, will not go unnoticed.

7. Warning: Old Batch Practitioners' Powers Have Been Renewed and May Feel Mor e Intense The speaker explains that returning practitioners' spiritual powers are being refreshed and changed roughly every 1 1 days throughout this sadhna, and that this renewed ener gy — described as high-intensity ener gies connected to Lord Shiva — may feel more intense than before.

8. Teaching: Even Lord Shiva's Energies Come First to Ram Bhakts The speaker states that Lord Shiva's ener gies are described as coming first and foremost to devotees of Ram, framing this sadhna's Shiva-associated powers as consistent with (not separate from) the group's Ram-centered devotion.

9. Practical Teaching: What to Do If You Feel "Dabna" (Pr essed/Stuck) in a Dr eam The speaker instructs that if a devotee feels stuck/pressed in a dream during this sadhna, they should chant the Jai Siyaram mantra within the dream state itself as the response to that experience.

10. Metaphor: The Ten Blankets — Understanding Dabna as a Counter -For ce, Not a Threat The speaker of fers an extended metaphor: piling on blanket after blanket for warmth (up to ten) eventually produces a sensation of being crushed by their weight; similarly , as a practitioner advances through levels of sadhna and gains additional spiritual "layers," a natural counter -force can make the accumulated weight feel suf focating — but the correct response is not to fight to remove the layers, but to work "outward/upward" through them gently rather than struggling against the full weight at once.

1 1. Teaching: When Facing Injustice, Let It Play Out to Its Extr eme The speaker teaches that when a devotee experiences what feels like significant injustice during this process, the right response is to observe how far it extends rather than resist — reasoning that an opposing spiritual force testing a devotee will eventually recognize that extremity has no ef fect and change its approach.

12. Teaching: Layer ed Dreams and the "Inception" Comparison The speaker compares the layered dream states experienced in advanced sadhna to the film "Inception" (dream within dream within dream), noting that most people can only follow up to four layers deep, as a way of introducing that this session's teaching on dimensions will explore similar layered structures.

13. Teaching: Second-Chapter Jaap Method — Vocal Mantra, Inward Focus, Sustained Gaze The speaker teaches the method for this stage of practice: chanting "Jai Siyaram" aloud with the mouth while silently holding "Ram" in the mind, maintaining a steady , unforced gaze toward the divine (not a harsh stare) for a sustained period (four hours), during which one's ener gies will shift over time as various saints visit and teach the practitioner .

14. Teaching: Track and Note All Bodily and Emotional Changes During This Sadhna The speaker instructs devotees to note every change in their body and mood during this period — including days of unusual depression followed by days of unusual clarity and understanding — reassuring them that such fluctuation is expected and not cause for alarm.

15. Light Exchange: On Enthusiasm and Absorbing Rather Than Interrupting When the speaker jokingly scolds the batch for seeming unenthusiastic and quiet, several devotees explain that their quietness reflects careful listening and absorption of new material (deliberately not interrupting with questions) rather than disinterest — the speaker accepts this explanation warmly .

16. Teaching: Even a Monkey (Bandar) Should Enjoy Some Play — Playfulness Is a Birthright The speaker teaches that having fun and playfulness is every devotee's natural birthright, using the phrase "a monkey who doesn't play is no monkey at all" and noting that the group's own guru (Hanuman ji Maharaj, "Kapiraj," lord of the monkeys) embodies exactly this playful spirit.

17. Lectur e Begins: Revisiting Shiva Tattva and Intr oducing Multi-Dimensional Theory The speaker announces that the session will revisit and deepen an earlier teaching on "Shiva Tattva" (previously taught only at a simplified level in the general Mool Tatva track), moving into a more rigorous, "scientific" explanation intended specifically for this advanced batch.

18. Teaching: Chakras and the First Dimension Using a devotee (Akhilesh) as a running illustrative example, the speaker teaches that a person's seven bodily chakras form their "first dimension," with kundalini shakti rising from the base and crossing each chakra in turn.

19. Teaching: Dimensions Incr ease With Chakra Count (14, 32, 64...) The speaker teaches that successive dimensions are associated with increasing numbers of chakras (14 in the second dimension, 32 in the next, 64 after that, and so on), each dimension representing a "floor" that a practitioner's ener gy can rise through.

20. Teaching: "Up" and "Down" Are Relative — There Is No Universal "Up" The speaker teaches, using multiple seated devotees as reference points, that "up" and "down" are relative to the observer's own position — what looks like descent from one person's frame of reference is simultaneously ascent from another's, meaning there is no single, universal "up" direction in this framework.

21. Teaching: Negative Displacement Is Only a Matter of Perspective, Not True Negativity Building on the previous point, the speaker teaches that what looks like "negative" spiritual movement is often simply a dif ference in observational frame, not a genuine spiritual setback — encouraging devotees not to panic over apparent regression that may , from another vantage point, be real progress.

22. Teaching: Kundalini Shakti and the Infinity Symbol The speaker describes the classic kundalini pathway (through ida and pingala nadis in a serpentine pattern) as forming, when reoriented horizontally , the mathematical infinity symbol — introducing this as the basis for the session's central metaphor .

23. Teaching: The Loophole of Repetition — Activating Both Nadis Still Keeps You in the Same Loop The speaker teaches that even fully activating both major nadis (ener gy channels) keeps a practitioner within the same closed "infinity loop," meaning that this particular pathway , however completely traveled, does not by itself take a practitioner beyond its own boundaries — a structural point the session builds on when explaining planetary/cosmic movement next.

24. Teaching: Earth's Rotation, Revolution, and the Illusion of Continuous Rising The speaker uses the Earth's simultaneous rotation and orbit around the sun (and the sun's own motion through the cosmos) to illustrate that a practitioner (again using Akhilesh as the example) can feel as though they are continuously rising in spiritual "dimension," while their net displacement, viewed from a wider frame, may return to zero — since the underlying cosmic path is itself a repeating loop.

25. Teaching: Two Practitioners on the Same "Plane" Shar e the Same Experience Regardless of Years Practiced The speaker teaches that spiritual experience depends on which "plane" a practitioner occupies, not on tenure — someone with forty years of sadhna and someone with four years can have identical experiences if they occupy the same plane, while practitioners on dif ferent planes will have dif ferent experiences even at the same tenure.

26. Teaching: The Loop (Infinity) Can Never Be Broken — Only the "Plane" Can Change The speaker states as a structural principle that the underlying "infinity" loop of this cosmic structure has never been broken by anyone, and cannot be — what a practitioner's sadhna can change is which plane they occupy within that same loop, not the loop's existence.

27. Teaching: Reconciling Scriptural Refer ences to the 10th and 14th Dimensions The speaker raises a deliberate tension for teaching purposes: scriptures describe fourteen realms (bhavans) and describe Lord Shiva as existing in a 10th dimension and Rama Sarkar/Prabhu Ram in a 14th dimension at Baikunth Dham — and asks the batch to consider how this squares with the "everything loops back to zero" principle just taught, framing this as a genuine puzzle to sit with rather than resolving it immediately .

28. Teaching: How Mantras Travel — First Through Planets, Then Across the Cosmos The speaker teaches that when a mantra is chanted, it first "builds a path" that a practitioner's kundalini shakti then follows; that path is described as extending outward planet by planet, and eventually crossing the dimensional structure of the wider cosmos.

29. Teaching: Why a Single Mantra Utterance Can Work Across All Realms (Law of Inertia) The speaker teaches that once a mantra's path has crossed every planetary/dimensional structure, its power becomes strong enough that a single utterance activates mantra-consciousness across the entire cosmos — meaning a practitioner's subtle bodies work simultaneously across every realm — and cites this "law of inertia" as the same mechanism previously taught for how Lord Krishna could produce a miracle in one realm by engaging his subtle body in many others simultaneously .

30. Teaching: The Progr essive Dimensional Powers of Mantra, First Through Higher Dimensions The speaker walks through a staged framework in which a mantra's reach expands with each additional dimension: in the first dimension, a mantra moves either forward or backward with great intensity; in the second (a time dimension), it can move forward or backward in time; in higher dimensions it additionally moves up/down, reaching into parallel planes; by the sixth dimension a mantra becomes "omnipresent" — active across every plane simultaneously; the seventh through ninth dimensions add spatial forward/backward and up/down movement together .

31. Teaching: Why Lord Shiva Is Described as Existing in the 10th Dimension, and Rama Sarkar in the 14th The speaker concludes the lecture by teaching that Lord Shiva's ability to utter ten mantras simultaneously in ten directions is why scripture places

him in the 10th dimension, while Rama Sarkar (Baikunth-dwelling Prabhu Ram) is placed in the 14th dimension for uttering fourteen mantras simultaneously — and states that the speaker's own guru, seated (in this framework) at the sixth dimension, has thereby "bound" the 14th-dimension Lord through devotion, referencing the line "Sumire pawan sut paavan naama, apne hi vas kari rakhe Rama."

32. Closing: "Aaj Ka Packup Done" — Session to Continue the Next Day The speaker ends the session by declaring the day's teaching complete, and, in response to a devotee whose formal sankalp had not yet been completed, tells them to continue their own personal sadhna and confirms the group will pick up again the next day .
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This session is an advanced "Third Eye" batch training session combining a sankalp roll call, a warning about the seriousness of an ongoing sadhna, teaching on "dabna" (dream paralysis) as a spiritual test, and an extended technical lecture on chakras, dimensions, and mantra mechanics. If a practitioner feels "dabna" (stuck/pressed) in a dream during this sadhna, the taught response is to chant Jai Siyaram within the dream itself; the "ten blankets" metaphor teaches that this pressure should be worked through gently rather than fought against. A devotee's guru is described as their spiritual tattva (essence); deceiving one's guru or harboring hidden dishonesty during this sadhna is described as certain to surface. Central technical teaching: dimensions are described as layered "planes," with "up" and "down" being relative to the observer rather than absolute; the underlying cosmic "infinity loop" cannot be broken by any practitioner — sadhna changes which plane a practitioner occupies within that loop, not the loop itself. A mantra's power is taught to expand with each dimension crossed: from simple forward/backward movement, to time travel, to full omnipresence (by the sixth dimension) and beyond; Lord Shiva is placed at the 10th dimension (uttering ten simultaneous mantras) and Rama Sarkar at the 14th (fourteen simultaneous mantras) within this specific teaching framework. This teaching is presented as a deepened, more technical version of an earlier , simplified "Shiva Tattva" lesson, intended specifically for this advanced batch rather than the general devotee audience. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 95, English)
The Third Eye Batch: Dabna, the Second-Chapter Sadhna, and the Teaching on Dimensions
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this advanced Thir d Eye batch training session.

Q1. What is "dabna" in the context of this sadhna? A: Per this teaching, "dabna" refers to a dream state in which a person realizes they are dreaming and wants to wake up or escape, but is unable to — described here specifically as being "pressed" or "stuck."
Q2. What should a practitioner do if they experience "dabna" during this sadhna? A: Per this teaching, the taught response is to chant the Jai Siyaram mantra within the dream itself.

Q3. What does the "ten blankets" metaphor teach about advancing thr ough sadhna? A: Per this teaching, as a practitioner gains additional spiritual "layers" through advancing sadhna, the accumulated weight can feel suf focating, similar to piling on ten blankets for warmth — the correct response is to work through the pressure gently rather than fighting to throw it all of f at once.

Q4. What should a devotee do when facing what feels like serious injustice during this sadhna? A: Per this teaching, the guidance is to observe how far the injustice extends rather than resist it directly , since an opposing force will eventually recognize that extremity produces no reaction and change its approach.

Q5. Is a devotee's guru described as important in this teaching? A: Yes — per this teaching, a devotee's guru is described as their spiritual tattva (essence), and deceiving one's guru or harboring hidden dishonesty during this sadhna is described as certain to surface.

Q6. Why might r eturning ("old batch") practitioners feel a mor e intense experience in this sadhna? A: Per this teaching, returning practitioners' spiritual powers are refreshed roughly every 1 1 days throughout this sadhna, and the renewed, high-intensity ener gies (associated with Lord Shiva) may feel stronger than before.

Q7. What is the method taught for this stage's jaap practice? A: Per this teaching, the method is to chant "Jai Siyaram" aloud with the mouth while silently holding "Ram" in the mind, maintaining a steady , unforced gaze toward the divine for a sustained period (around four hours).

Q8. Should a practitioner be alarmed by mood swings (like sudden depr ession) during this sadhna? A: No — per this teaching, practitioners are told to simply note all bodily and emotional changes, including days of unusual depression followed by days of unusual clarity , as an expected part of the process rather than cause for alarm.

Q9. What ar e "dimensions" according to this teaching's framework? A: Per this teaching, dimensions are described as layered "planes" through which a practitioner's spiritual ener gy can rise, with "up" and "down" being relative to the observer's own position rather than absolute directions.

Q10. Does appar ent "negative" spiritual movement always mean a r eal setback? A: No — per this teaching, what looks like negative displacement is often simply a dif ference in observational frame rather than genuine spiritual regression.

Q1 1. What is the significance of the infinity symbol in this teaching? A: Per this teaching, the kundalini pathway through the ida and pingala nadis, when reoriented, forms the mathematical infinity symbol — illustrating that even fully activating both nadis keeps a practitioner within the same closed cosmic "loop."

Q12. Can this cosmic "loop" ever be broken by a practitioner's sadhna? A: No — per this teaching, the underlying infinity loop has never been broken by anyone and cannot be; what sadhna changes is which "plane" a practitioner occupies within that same loop.

Q13. Does years of practice guarantee a mor e advanced spiritual experience than someone with less experience? A: Not necessarily — per this teaching, experience depends on which "plane" a practitioner occupies, not tenure; a practitioner with forty years and one with four years can have identical experiences if they share the same plane.

Q14. How does this teaching explain the way a chanted mantra "travels"? A: Per this teaching, a mantra first builds a path that the practitioner's kundalini shakti then follows, extending outward planet by planet before crossing the wider cosmic dimensional structure.

Q15. How can a single mantra utterance be effective acr oss many r ealms at once? A: Per this teaching, once a mantra's path has crossed the full planetary/dimensional structure, its power becomes strong enough that a single utterance activates mantraconsciousness across the entire cosmos simultaneously — described using a "law of inertia" analogy also applied to Krishna's miracles.

Q16. According to this teaching's staged framework, what changes about a mantra's r each as dimensions incr ease? A: Per this teaching, in the first dimension a mantra moves forward or backward with intensity; in the second, it can move forward/backward in time; higher dimensions add up/down movement into parallel planes; by the sixth dimension it becomes fully omnipresent across all planes; the seventh through ninth dimensions add combined spatial movement.

Q17. Why is Lord Shiva associated with the 10th dimension in this teaching? A: Per this teaching, Lord Shiva's ability to utter ten mantras simultaneously in ten directions is given as the reason scripture places him in the 10th dimension.

Q18. Why is Rama Sarkar associated with the 14th dimension in this teaching? A: Per this teaching, Rama Sarkar (Baikunthdwelling Prabhu Ram) is placed in the 14th dimension for uttering fourteen mantras simultaneously .

Q19. Is having fun and playfulness discouraged during serious sadhna practice, per this teaching? A: No — per this teaching, playfulness is described as every devotee's natural birthright, illustrated by the phrase "a monkey who doesn't play is no monkey at all" and the group's own guru, Hanuman ji Maharaj ("Kapiraj"), embodying that same playful spirit.

Q20. How did this session close? A: Per this teaching, the speaker declared the day's lecture complete ("aaj ka packup done"), told a devotee whose formal sankalp hadn't yet finished to continue their personal sadhna, and confirmed the group would reconvene the next day .
Bot Response Guidelines

Present the dimensional/mantra-physics framework (Q9–Q18) as this specific advanced-batch teaching's own internal framework, clearly distinct from mainstream physics terminology it borrows language from (dimensions, parallel universes, inertia) — do not present it as scientific consensus. Present the opening kaal sarp dosh note (Section 1 of the Knowledge Base) as directed at an unnamed individual continuing a prior private conversation; do not speculate about who it refers to. This session is specifically for the "Third Eye" advanced batch — note this context if a user asks whether this teaching applies to general Ashaeiynn practice. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Q&A (Session 95, Hinglish)
The Third Eye Batch: Dabna, the Second-Chapter Sadhna, and the Teaching on Dimensions

This is NOT an exhaustive transcript of every exchange in this session. Only conversations judged genuinely valuable and likely to benefit futur e users ar e included, each with a short italicized note explaining why it was kept. This session is lar gely dir ect instruction, so Part III her e is shorter than in sessions with mor e open sangat conversation.
Exchange 1 — "Wher e Can We Find Reference Material?"

Devotee: Bhaiya, aap jo bhi padhate ho reference bhi dete ho, aapne bola bhi hai ki aap ye source... aap kuch aisa bhi hai jo hum baad mein padh bhi sakte hain apne aap se ya reference kahin check kar sakte hain? Koi bhi aisa book ho ya aapse kuch aur mile jo hum dekh sakein baad mein, kuch explain na hua ho achhe se agar woh samajhna ho? Bhaiya: Toh phir se aa jao Third Eye batch mein, phir sikhayenge. 1 1 baar karenge ek saath sadhna — 1 1 baar mein saala kabhi toh samajh aayega. Isi bahaane tumhari sadhna ho jaayegi bhaiyon. Isi bahaane tumhari saadhna ho jaayegi. Aur 1 1 baar padhna aur 1 1 baar sadhna mein — vachan deta hoon, jab tak tum is sadhna ko poori karoge tab tak tumhe har tarike ki shaktiyan tumhare paas hongi.

Why this is her e: A practical, honest answer to a question many advanced students would genuinely have (is ther e a r eference text?) — the r esponse r eframes r epetition itself as the "r eference material," which is a distinctive teaching appr oach worth pr eserving.
Exchange 2 — The "No Enthusiasm" Scolding

Bhaiya: Arre is batch mein itna enthusiasm hai hi nahi, mujhe woh nahi dikh raha, warna toh har batch mein itna... aise bhaiya aaj seekhenge, aaj kuch milega... ye sab rotdu mile hain mujhe is batch mein. Devotee: Nahi Bhaiya, hum log wait karte rehte hain, aap kuch batayein hum sune. Devotee 2: Bade interest ke saath session join kiya hai aur chup isliye hain kyunki cheezon ko absorb kar rahe hain — sab cheezon ko absorb kar rahe hain, sab sun rahe hain jo aap samjhate ho. Aisa nahi ki saari cheezein samajh aati hain, kuch cheezein sar ke upar se nikal rahi hain but kuch cheezein samajh aa jaati hain. Bhaiya: Achha, extra excited hai na? Excited hai. Haan bhai excited hai.

Why this is her e: A warm, human moment that shows how students genuinely engage with dense material — r eassuring for anyone worried that quiet attentiveness during a session might be r ead as disinter est.
Exchange 3 — "But What About Negative Dimensions?"

Devotee: Bhaiya isme negative dimension bhi hoti hai na, toh ye dimension ko hum level nahi consider kar sakte kya, jaise 12th standard ya aise kuch? Bhaiya: Abhi maine ye samjhaya ki ye jo neeche baitha hai, woh jab isko dekhega — kyunki iska sar yahan pe hai, iska sar yahan pe hai — ye jab isko dekhega toh A upar wali side ko A ko dekhega toh usko lagega ki ye neeche ja raha hai. Par
actual mein woh upar chadh raha hai wahan pe, kyunki woh idhar baitha hai, iski mundi idhar hai. Toh negative dimension kahin bhi nahi hui — ye sirf dekhne ka nazariya hai.

Why this is her e: A sharp, clarifying student question that catches a natural point of confusion in the dimension framework, and the answer dir ectly resolves it — useful for anyone trying to follow the logic of "r elative up and down" taught in this session.
Note on Curation

The long sankalp roll call of devotee names was left out of this curated section entirely , since it is a routine attendance/commitment ritual rather than a conversation with independent teaching value (it is described in Part I instead). Most of this session consists of sustained, uninterrupted lecture on dimensions and mantra mechanics; that material is captured in full in Part I and Part II rather than reproduced here as dialogue.
